prompt: What is TOGAF's unit of work, by the lesson?
hint: Not a system.

choices.text: One software system and its containers
choices.why: That is lesson 3's level; TOGAF works across the portfolio.

choices.text: A change to the enterprise
choices.why: Right: such as every passenger boarding with a digital ticket by 2027.

choices.text: A sprint of the delivery teams
choices.why: TOGAF has no notion of sprints; its series guides discuss working with agile delivery.

choices.text: A single diagram in ArchiMate
choices.why: ArchiMate is the notation; TOGAF says what to produce, not how to draw it.

prompt: Which of these does the lesson say TOGAF is not? Choose all that apply.
hint: Notation, an end-to-end run, and code.

choices.text: A notation for drawing
choices.why: Yes: that is ArchiMate's job.

choices.text: A methodology to run end to end without changes
choices.why: Yes: the standard asks for it to be tailored.

choices.text: Specific to software changes
choices.why: Yes: a reorganisation or a new supplier is a change too.

choices.text: A framework for enterprise architecture
choices.why: That is exactly what it is.

prompt: Match each Carcará item to its TOGAF architecture domain.
hint: Business, data, application, technology.

prompt: Which domain does the C4 model of lesson 3 leave out, by this lesson?
hint: The layer above the systems.

choices.text: Technology, because C4 has no infrastructure
choices.why: C4's deployment diagram covers technology.

choices.text: Business
choices.why: Right: capabilities and processes sit above what C4 draws.

choices.text: Application, because C4 is about code
choices.why: Context and container diagrams are application architecture.

choices.text: Data, since C4 leaves databases unnamed
choices.why: Container diagrams name databases and what they hold.

prompt: This is the ADM ring with its letters and names removed. Put each phase on its circle.
hint: The cycle runs clockwise from the top right, and two phases are not on the ring.

prompt: Put these ADM phases in the order of the cycle.
hint: Vision, the three architectures, then solutions, migration, governance and change.
trap: Migration planning comes after the solutions are identified, not before.

prompt: In Phase D, Carcará found that station links cannot carry a full sale when they drop. What does the ADM say should happen?
hint: The centre of the ring.

choices.text: Finish Phase D and fix it in the next cycle
choices.why: The ADM expects loops inside a cycle when something found later changes an earlier decision.

choices.text: Log it centrally; revisit Phase B
choices.why: Yes: it went into Requirements Management at the centre and sent Phase B back, which produced the offline sale mode.

choices.text: Escalate it to the architecture board for a dispensation
choices.why: A dispensation is for a project that cannot conform, not for a new requirement.

choices.text: Drop the stations from the scope
choices.why: The stations are the point of the change.

prompt: Which phase produced the answer for passengers with no phone and no e-mail?
hint: It was not an engineer's answer.

choices.text: Phase D, Technology
choices.why: Technology kept the printers; the decision to print a QR receipt was a business one.

choices.text: Phase B, Business Architecture
choices.why: Right: the gap analysis found the passenger, and the business answer was a QR receipt.

choices.text: Phase G, Implementation Governance
choices.why: Governance checks conformance; it does not design the service.

choices.text: Phase F, Migration Planning
choices.why: Migration ordered the work; the receipt was decided earlier.

prompt: What did Carcará's Statement of Architecture Work contain, by the lesson?
hint: Two pages for the board.

choices.text: The full target architecture in four domains
choices.why: That is the Architecture Definition Document, produced in B to D.

choices.text: The decision records of the programme so far
choices.why: Records are written as decisions are made, later.

choices.text: Scope, vision and success
choices.why: Yes: scope, stakeholders, the vision, the constraints and the measure of success, enough for the board to agree before money was spent.

choices.text: The migration plan by quarter
choices.why: That came out of Phase F.

prompt: In the gap matrix, the station back office is eliminated. What question must be asked of it?
hint: On purpose, or forgotten?

choices.text: Which team will delete its code
choices.why: A practical step that comes after the real question.

choices.text: How much it cost to build
choices.why: Sunk cost does not decide whether its capabilities are needed.

choices.text: Whether it can be kept running in parallel forever
choices.why: That would avoid the elimination, not examine it.

choices.text: Was its loss deliberate?
choices.why: Right: the check found the cash refunds and the end-of-day cash report.

prompt: Why does the lesson say transition architectures are often the most complicated ones?
hint: Two stations on the target, twenty-four on the baseline.

choices.text: Both old and new must work, side by side
choices.why: Yes: a passenger who buys at a pilot station and boards at another must still board.

choices.text: Because they use newer technology
choices.why: The complexity is in coexistence, not in novelty.

choices.text: Because TOGAF requires twelve of them
choices.why: There is no fixed number; Carcará had three.

choices.text: Because they are drawn in a different notation
choices.why: They are described like any architecture.

prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
hint: What versus how; generic versus specific.

pairs.right: a needed capability, independent of product
how a capability is provided, with a product or component
where principles, models and decisions live
a classification from generic to organisation-specific

right_distractors: a meeting of the team leads

prompt: A principle reads: Boarding works without a network. Which part makes it usable by a reviewer?
hint: A principle without it is a slogan.

choices.text: Its name
choices.why: The name helps people refer to it; it does not guide a decision.

choices.text: Its rationale, the 40% of stops with poor signal
choices.why: The rationale says why; the reviewer needs to know what follows.

choices.text: The implications
choices.why: Right: every boarding feature needs an offline design and a sync rule.

choices.text: The date it was approved
choices.why: Useful for history, not for applying it.

prompt: A building block that says what capability is needed, independent of any product, is an ___ building block.
hint: The ABB.

prompt: The pilot stations kept their old PCs for one quarter. What made that governance rather than drift?
hint: An exception with an end date.

choices.text: The board did not notice it
choices.why: An unnoticed exception is drift.

choices.text: The teams agreed it among themselves in chat
choices.why: An agreement nobody can find is not a decision of record.

choices.text: A dated, recorded dispensation
choices.why: Yes: it was closed when the tablets arrived.

choices.text: The PCs were cheap to keep
choices.why: Cost was not what made it governed.

prompt: What separates a board that is a gate from a board that is a standard, by the lesson?
hint: Can the teams predict its answers?

choices.text: How often it meets
choices.why: Frequency matters less than whether its answers are predictable.

choices.text: Predictable answers
choices.why: Right: when teams can predict its answers from the written principles, it is a standard; a board that surprises teams at the end is a gate.

choices.text: Whether the CTO chairs it
choices.why: Who chairs it does not make its decisions predictable.

choices.text: Whether it uses the full compliance scale
choices.why: The lesson says the finer grades are more than most organisations need.

prompt: Which parts of TOGAF did Carcará keep? Choose all that apply.
hint: Each kept part answered a real question.

choices.text: Baseline, target and gap analysis
choices.why: Yes: it found the capabilities the target forgot.

choices.text: Transition architectures
choices.why: Yes: 26 stations could not switch in one day.

choices.text: The full content metamodel in a repository tool
choices.why: Skipped, and the skip was written down.

choices.text: Principles with implications
choices.why: Yes: they let teams predict the board.

prompt: What question does the lesson ask of every TOGAF deliverable?
hint: A reader and an action.

choices.text: Who reads it, and to do what?
choices.why: Yes: ask who reads it and what they do differently because of it; if nobody, skip it and write down that you did.

choices.text: Does the standard require it?
choices.why: The standard itself asks for tailoring.

choices.text: Can a tool generate it automatically?
choices.why: Generating an unread document is still waste.

choices.text: Will the certification exam ask about it?
choices.why: Exams test knowledge of the framework, not what a company needs.

prompt: An interviewer asks what you know of TOGAF. What does the lesson say a good interviewer wants to hear?
hint: Not the list of phases.

choices.text: The names of the ten phases, in order, from memory
choices.why: A recital shows memory, not judgement.

choices.text: Your certification level
choices.why: A signal, not an answer to what you would do.

choices.text: What each part solves, and what you'd leave out
choices.why: Right: the judgement to tailor it to an organisation.

choices.text: That TOGAF is outdated and agile replaces it
choices.why: That dismisses the parts that pay for themselves, which Carcará kept.

prompt: Carcará's programme has 26 stations. The first transition architecture covers two pilot stations. How many stations still run the baseline at the end of that quarter?
hint: Stations minus pilots.
